title: Slim down routing layer and remove legacy shims
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Over several product iterations we accumulated multiple small shims and compatibility layers in the smart routing stack (policy adapters, legacy fallback hooks, and region-affinity decorators). These have increased CPU overhead on the hotpath, complicated reasoning about fallback invariants, and made changes to regional lease logic risky. This ticket scopes a targeted cleanup to remove the legacy shim layers, replace them with a single thin adapter surface, and harden the fallback choreography so that regional failover remains predictable under load. The goal is reduce p99 routing CPU by ~25% for large multi-tenant bursts and eliminate two sources of flakey behavior seen in the incident logs from 2026-01.
acceptance_criteria: 1) All legacy shims removed and replaced by the thin adapter surface documented in the design doc. 2) Unit and integration tests updated; CI coverage >= 95% for modified packages. 3) End-to-end routing latency p95 reduced by at least 15% and p99 by at least 20% in the synthetic multi-tenant benchmark. 4) Fallbacks are deterministic: recorded test harness reproduces a regional failover with identical decision traces before and after the rollout (except for expected latency improvements). 5) No customer-facing errors introduced; canary shows zero increase in 5xx for 48 hours. 6) Code passes security review and the change log is added to the release notes.
tasks: Audit: catalogue all shim entry points and callsites across router-service and policy-engine (ENG-171824)
Design: finalize thin adapter interface and invariants (confluence: /pages/Routing/Adapter-Design)
Refactor: implement adapter and migrate two most-trafficked shims behind feature flag (DEV-branch)
Testing: update unit tests, add integration test harness for regional failover scenarios
Benchmark: run synthetic multi-tenant burst benchmark and capture before/after traces
Rollout: gated canary with rollback hooks and monitoring dashboards
Postmortem: capture lessons and update routing playbook
implementation_notes: We will introduce a single Adapter trait in go/routing/adapter with three explicit primitives: EvaluatePolicy(ctx, request) -> decision, ReserveRegionLease(ctx, tenant) -> leaseToken, and EmitFallback(ctx, decision, reason). The legacy shim layers (policy compat, per-tenant overrides, old fallback hooks) will be ported to call these primitives and then removed. Use non-blocking channels for lease reservation to avoid adding latency to the EvaluatePolicy hotpath. Keep the feature flag behind runtime config 'routing.adapter_migration' and add metrics: adapter_eval_time_ms, adapter_lease_wait_ms, adapter_fallback_count. The migration must not alter the serialized decision proto format seen by downstream workers. Coordinate with infra to ensure canary traffic is routed to test cluster. Use a short-lived branch and open one PR per package to keep reviews small.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: subtle semantic drift in fallback ordering could change which model variant gets selected under contention. Mitigation: add decision-trace integration tests and a golden harness that asserts deterministic ordering; run decision-replay across 100k historical routing events. Risk: lease reservation could become a bottleneck and increase p99 latency. Mitigation: implement optimistic fast-path for cache hits and use a background replenishment thread for leases. Risk: rollout triggers a race with older Dedicated nodes. Mitigation: add compatibility shim for version negotiation; disable the removal behind a config until fleet reaches >= runtime-1.18.
qa_plan: 1) Unit tests for adapter primitives and migrated shims. 2) Integration: spin up local routing cluster with synthetic tenants and induce region outages to verify deterministic fallbacks. 3) Load test: run the multi-tenant burst benchmark at 3x expected peak to stress lease logic. 4) Canary: deploy to canary cluster (5% traffic) for 48h with automatic rollback if 5xx increase > 0.1% or latency regressions exceed thresholds. 5) Post-deploy: run replay of 10k historical routing decisions and compare traces.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature-flagged branch merged to main and internal QA completes. Phase 1: Enable flag for internal canary traffic (~5%) and monitor metrics for 48 hours. Phase 2: Gradually increase to 25% with safety gates at each step. Phase 3: Full rollout and remove legacy shim code paths one package at a time, with short rollback windows. Communicate schedule in #infra-routing and update runbooks. Coordinate with Dedicated ops for a coordinated deployment window to avoid cross-version interactions.
